behavior_anomalies.why: The log shows flu patients continuing to accumulate but never shows the expected consequence of zero ventilators—no ventilation allocation, denial, diversion, or other handling for patients who depend on ventilators.

The log begins adding flu patients despite the hospital having zero functional ventilators, but it never shows the expected consequence for patients dependent on ventilation—such as inability to ventilate, deterioration, or deaths.

After the log reaches zero available and functional ventilators at t6, the patient population continues growing without any recorded consequence for patients who depend on ventilators—such as unmet ventilation demand or denied treatment. No ventilator orders or replacement capacity appear either.
After all ventilators reach zero at t6, the log continues adding patients but never shows any patients being denied ventilation, left unmet, or otherwise affected by the loss of ventilator capacity.

After both ventilator resources reach zero, the log never shows the expected consequence that ventilator-dependent admissions or care stop. The repeated 'admit-patients' behavior therefore appears not to be constrained by the exhausted ventilator capacity.

After the log sets available and functional ventilators to 0 at t6, it shows no consequence for patients who need ventilation. The model continues increasing the patient population without recording denial of ventilation, alternative treatment, transfer, or mortality.

After "hospital.hospital_capacity.functional_ventilators 1->0" at t6, the log continues adding patients but never records the expected consequence for patients dependent on ventilation—such as inability to allocate ventilation, deterioration, or deaths.
The ventilator resources are exhausted, but the log never shows ventilation stopping, patients becoming unable to receive ventilation, or unmet ventilator demand.

The ventilator resource is exhausted, but the log never records the expected consequence for patients who depend on it—stopping new ventilation or documenting denial/triage of ventilator-supported care.

After all ventilators reached zero at t6, the log continues adding patients but never shows any consequence for patients dependent on ventilatory support—such as inability to ventilate, triage, or an outcome for those patients.

The ventilator resource is exhausted, but the log never shows the dependent consequence: patients being unable to receive ventilation or release-ventilation becoming ineffective. Flu demand continues increasing, with no indication that the zero-capacity condition affects ventilation.

After ventilator capacity reaches zero at t6, the log continues increasing patient demand but never records any consequence for patients who depend on ventilators, such as waiting, denial of ventilation, or deterioration/death.

action admit-flu-patients-v1 refuses up front with check 'the hospital has enough available beds' on actor.components.hospital_capacity.available_beds, a stock the actor's own activity consumes. Fix with three changes: (1) the action only STARTS the activity (sets a status such as 'driving'), with no check on that stock and no progress or consumption effects; (2) add a process that, every tick while the status is active and the stock is above zero, makes one tick of progress and consumes the stock; (3) add a process that switches the status to a stopped/failed value when the stock is at or below zero, so the actor discovers it by observation.
